Riff

Voice agent platform that generates deterministic FSM-based voice agents from plain English business descriptions.

https://github.com/davidbmar/riff  ·  private  ·  shipped

📄 Project documentation (50 docs) →

What it is

A Python-based platform for building voice agents where an LLM handles natural language generation while a declared YAML state graph enforces business logic, slot validation, and transition guards. It separates the 'riff' (LLM creativity) from the 'beat' (deterministic state management) to prevent hallucinations in phone conversations.

Features

  • Generates voice agent flows from plain English business descriptions
  • Enforces deterministic state transitions using YAML-defined graphs
  • Prevents LLM hallucinations via slot validation and guardrails
  • Supports multiple LLM backends including Gemini, Gemma, and Claude
  • Includes built-in flows for common services like plumbing and salons
  • Provides a web UI for real-time conversation inspection and debugging

Quickstart

cd ~/src/riff
.venv/bin/python3 -m pytest tests/ -q
.venv/bin/python3 -m riff.web_server

How it's built

Built with Python using a modular architecture. Core components include a YAML flow loader, a pure-function state manager, guardrails layers, and adapters for STT/TTS/LLM providers (Gemini, Gemma, Claude). It uses a web server for API and UI, and JSONL for logging. The system relies on deterministic pure functions for all logic except the LLM call itself.

How it runs

sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller
    participant STT
    participant WebServer
    participant RunTurn
    participant StateManager
    participant LLM
    participant TTS
    Caller->>STT: Speak audio
    STT->>WebServer: Send transcribed text
    WebServer->>RunTurn: Invoke run_turn
    RunTurn->>StateManager: Get current state
    StateManager-->>RunTurn: Return state context
    RunTurn->>LLM: Generate response
    LLM-->>RunTurn: Return raw text
    RunTurn->>StateManager: Validate transitions
    StateManager-->>RunTurn: Confirm valid transition
    RunTurn->>TTS: Synthesize audio
    TTS-->>WebServer: Return audio stream
    WebServer-->>Caller: Play audio response

How to apply & reuse

Use riff to rapidly prototype and deploy voice agents for service businesses (plumbing, dental, salons) or retail (coffee, pizza). Describe the business logic in plain English via the API to generate a flow, then integrate the resulting voice endpoint into phone systems or test via the provided web UI.
